Without getting into the dumb/controversial story elements, the game runs horribly. I play co-op with my homeboy, the game crashes constantly, lags like a mf'r, and has connectivity issues all the time. The constant 40-50 GB updates eat up my storage space (ya ya I know hard drive this and that), and updating my graphics card once a week gets old. Outside of the constantly updating and crashing, the game play is fun and interesting. The controls work well and sometimes do what you want (locking on to cover etc.). The dynamic collapsing of the city is amazing, seeing Kalona fall to ruin in real time is great. With that being said you can just about beat the game with literally the DMR and the sniper. Every enemy is a bullet sponge other than the little imp dudes on the ground. I mean FFS the devs didn't even render rounds hitting the water. Its a small thing, but it shows the level of attention and care to detail. The collectibles and their sheer amount ALONGSIDE the gear box's are insane. I get wanting people to explore the map and that's a good way to do it, but it turns into a fetch quest for usable gear. I want to love the game (and the gameplay is decently fun), but dear lord let it die. I get people wanting to nostalgically play GOW, but this game just didn't hit the mark for me (outside of it not f***ing running).

This game is good as hell other than the fairly consistent crashing. I'm very happy with my purchase after finishing the campaign, and playing a bit of MP and Horde. A bit light on weapon specific executions though.

Performance is good for me, other than the crashing. I really hope they fix that soon.

This review only concerns the multiplayer. The campaign is okay, although I’ve always thought the one in Gears 2 was the best.

First of all, there are only four multiplayer maps. You can’t choose the game modes; they’re selected by a vote at the end of each match. Ranked mode isn’t available at launch—why not? Some of the multiplayer maps are far too big. That’s fine for Team Deathmatch, but not for the other modes.

Why aren’t modes from other Gears games, like Execution, included? Horde mode is okay, but the classic Horde mode is missing, where you fight wave after wave of increasingly powerful enemies. There’s also hardly any equipment, such as fences or towers, that you can upgrade.

I have to say, I found the multiplayer in Gears 5 even better—and that was already a downgrade.

-Each stage feels exactly the same until the last few stages.
-Graphical fidelity is VERY poor. What I mean by that is the environment is not 'alive'. There is no reacting with it. There is no wind, no raid, when walking through water there is no ripple effect yet they added water sound when you walk through it....trees do not move at all, no wind ever, just very static and dead feeling...generic...maybe is the right word. The graphics work but yeah imo very poor on bells and whistles in 2026.
- you could have cut out 8 or so levels entirely and it would not have been noticed. Its a little long for what it is.

I would recommend on heavy sale or if you just want to pal it up with four friends in a wack-a-mole shooter and not much else you might enjoy it.

I can't get past the horrible keyboard/mouse controls and keybinds. The keyboard/mouse bindings are directly mapped to the current controller layout. So not only do multiple actions have to be bound to the same button despite being separately listed in the keybindings, but they also change automatically if you switch the controller layout.

Player movement in general feels like you're playing at 300 ping at all times, and the camera locks when sprinting.

The game feels like I'm still playing an open beta. It has lots of potential, but it isn't for me in its current state.

I can only recommend buying the game if it's on sale, given that it only kinda works half the time.

Technical issues aside, I had researched the game on release and knew about the "woke" story/boring and repetitive game-play arguments but wanted to give it a chance and formulate my own opinions based off of my experience.
